title.value: Using incorpoRATE to examine clinician willingness to engage in shared decision making: A study of Family Medicine residents
title.justification: The paper evaluates clinicians' willingness to engage in shared decision making (SDM) using the incorpoRATE measure, focusing on Family Medicine residents.
title.quote: We evaluated the willingness of Family Medicine residents to engage in SDM, before and after an educational intervention.

extractions.description: This paper investigates the willingness of Family Medicine residents to engage in shared decision making (SDM) before and after an educational intervention. The study uses the incorpoRATE measure to assess changes in willingness over time, highlighting variability among residents and analyzing specific domains affecting SDM engagement. This research aims to provide insights for educators on improving training curricula in SDM.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on medical education and clinician practices, specifically shared decision making in clinical settings, without directly addressing climate or ecological sustainable development themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our aim in this study was to examine the willingness of FM residents to engage in SDM, before and after an educational intervention.

primary_category.justification: The central theme of the paper is medical education and clinical communication, which does not align with the predefined categories of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: This research did not examine clinical behavior or patient outcomes.

secondary_categories.justification: There is no indication in the paper that it addresses any secondary themes related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_categories.quote: None of these studies used validated measures of physician attitude to implementing SDM. To our knowledge, the willingness of Family Medicine (FM) residents to engage in SDM has not been evaluated.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not fit into any of the sub-categories related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_sub_category.quote: This study used a version of incorpoRATE that was recently adapted by the measure authors to improve item clarity and consistency of comprehension.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: As the paper does not cover Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development themes, no secondary sub-categories are applicable.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We calculated the total incorpoRATE score for each individual participant by summing each person’s individual item scores.

applications.justification: The paper is centered on shared decision-making in clinical training, not on applications related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
applications.quote: Among the 44 participants who completed incorpoRATE at both time points, the mean scores were 7.0 ± 1.0 at T1 and 7.4 ± 1.0 at T2.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper's focus on medical education and shared decision making does not align with the need for a new Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development category.
new_primary_category.quote: In follow-up to this study, future research should attempt to correlate the willingness to engage in SDM with observational measures of SDM.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The content of the paper, focused on medical education, does not require the creation of a new sub-category under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our findings map resident attitudes towards shared decision making at two time points, offering insights for refining educational methods.
